greek: Αδαμ δὲ ἔγνω Ευαν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτεκεν τὸν Καιν καὶ εἶπεν Ἐκτησάμην ἄνθρωπον διὰ τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: The name Cain explains itself in Hebrew and not in Greek.

notes.text: γινώσκω, *to learn to know, perceive*: the verb the Hebrew *yādaʿ* uses of a man's union with his wife, and the Greek keeps it — the verb of knowing good and evil at 2:17 and 3:5.
συλλαμβάνω's first sense is *to collect, gather together*; *to conceive*, of women, is its fourth. The headword keeps the lexicon's order, and the chain ends where the verse means.

κτάομαι, *to procure for oneself, to get, gain, acquire*. [[flag]] The Hebrew names *Qayin* from *qānîtî*, *I have gotten*. The Greek keeps the sense and loses the sound, so the name no longer explains itself.
*Through God.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾet-YHWH*, *with YHWH*, and uses the divine name; the Greek has θεός, with a preposition of agency.
Here the Greek transliterates the name it translated at 3:20: Hebrew *Ḥawwâ*, which was Ζωή there, is Ευα here, Ευαν in the accusative. The play on *life* is not made again.
Αδαμ is glossed again, first in this chapter. Καιν is Hebrew *Qayin*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αδαμ]] [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Ευαν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of him, and [[having collected|having collected, having gathered together, having taken up, having laid hold of and seized, having comprehended, having conceived]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] [[name:Καιν]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[I procured for myself|I procured for myself, I got, I gained, I acquired]] [[man|a man, a human being]] [[through|through, right through, by means of, by the agency of]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]].

names.gloss: (Ευαν, from Hebrew Ḥawwâ, which 3:20 translated Ζωή, "life")
(Καιν, from Hebrew Qayin, which the verse ties to qānâ, "to get, acquire")

greek: καὶ προσέθηκεν τεκεῖν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ τὸν Αβελ. καὶ ἐγένετο Αβελ ποιμὴν προβάτων, Καιν δὲ ἦν ἐργαζόμενος τὴν γῆν.
hint: The lexicon's first sense for the word Abel's flock is named by is 'anything that walks forward'.

notes.text: *Put to bearing*: προστίθημι with an infinitive, a Hebraism for doing a thing again, *wattōsep lāledet*. The lexicon's first sense is *to put to*; *to add* is its third.

Middle Liddell has no ποιμήν — only the Doric ποιμάν, a cross-reference to the entry the abridgement lacks — so the sense is LSJ's: *herdsman*, then *shepherd*, citing this verse. πρόβατον is, in the lexicon's own word, *properly* *anything that walks forward*: cattle and flocks in Homer, horses in Herodotus, and in Attic always sheep.
Hebrew *Hebel*, *breath, vapour*, a word used elsewhere for what is empty. The transliteration keeps only the sound.
Imperfect with a participle: *was working* — Cain's occupation as a continuing state, beside ἐγένετο for Abel's.

reading: and [[put to|put to, handed over and delivered, gave and bestowed, imposed further, attributed, added]] [[to bring into the world|to bring into the world, to bring forth, to bear, to produce]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of him [[name:Αβελ]]. and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[name:Αβελ]] [[herdsman|herdsman, shepherd, captain and chief, master and lord, pastor and teacher]] [[of anything that walks forward|of anything that walks forward, of cattle, of flocks and herds, of horses, of small cattle, of sheep]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Καιν]] was, and kept on being, [[working|working, labouring, working at and making and building, doing and performing and accomplishing, working the land, earning by working]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο μεθʼ ἡμέρας ἤνεγκεν Καιν ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τῆς γῆς θυσίαν τῷ κυρίῳ,
hint: The Hebrew has one word for both brothers' offerings; the Greek has two.

notes.text: θυσία is *an offering*, then *sacrifices, sacred rites*, then *the victim*. [[flag]] The Hebrew calls both offerings *minḥâ*, a gift. The Greek gives Cain's θυσία, here and at 4:5, and Abel's δῶρα at 4:4 — two words where the Hebrew has one.
*After days*; Hebrew *miqqēṣ yāmîm*, *at the end of days*. μετά with the accusative opens at *into the middle of*; *after*, of time, comes later in the entry.
φέρω, *to bear, carry*; *to bring, offer, present* stands further into the entry.

reading: and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] [[bore|bore, carried, bore along, brought and fetched, brought and offered and presented]] [[name:Καιν]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the fruits|of the fruits, of the produce, of the returns and profits, of the results]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] [[an offering|an offering, a mode of offering, offerings and sacrifices and sacred rites, a festival, the victim]] [[to the lord|to the lord, to the master, to the one having power and authority over]],

greek: καὶ Αβελ ἤνεγκεν καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπὸ τῶν πρωτοτόκων τῶν προβάτων αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν στεάτων αὐτῶν. καὶ ἐπεῖδεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ Αβελ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ,
hint: Hebrews quotes the phrase for Abel's gifts word for word.

notes.text: Hebrews 11:4 takes the phrase word for word — μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ — and calls Abel's offering θυσία, the word this chapter keeps for Cain's.
ἐφοράω, *to oversee, observe*, and of the gods *to watch over, take notice of*. The Hebrew *wayyišaʿ* is *he looked with regard*. Neither language says why.
Middle Liddell gives πρωτότοκος one sense, *first-born*, so it stands as plain text; στέαρ is *stiff fat, tallow, suet*.
καί as *also*: he too brought.

reading: and [[name:Αβελ]] [[bore|bore, carried, bore along, brought and fetched, brought and offered and presented]] also he [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] of the first-born [[of anything that walks forward|of anything that walks forward, of cattle, of flocks and herds, of horses, of small cattle, of sheep]] of him and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the stiff fats|of the stiff fats, of the tallow, of the suet]] of them. and [[oversaw|oversaw, observed, surveyed, watched over and took notice of, looked upon and beheld]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[name:Αβελ]] and [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the gifts|the gifts, the presents, the votive gifts, the blessings]] of him,

greek: ἐπὶ δὲ Καιν καὶ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις αὐτοῦ οὐ προσέσχεν. καὶ ἐλύπησεν τὸν Καιν λίαν, καὶ συνέπεσεν τῷ προσώπῳ.
hint: In Hebrew Cain burns with anger; in Greek he is grieved.

notes.text: λυπέω, *to give pain to, distress, grieve*. [[flag]] The Hebrew has *wayyiḥar lĕqayin*, *it burned to Cain* — anger — and at 4:6 asks *why are you angry?* The Greek makes it grief both times: ἐλύπησεν here, περίλυπος, *deeply grieved*, there.
No subject is named: *it grieved Cain*.
προσέχω's first sense is *to hold to, offer*; *to turn one's mind to, give heed to* follows. God did not turn to Cain's offering.
*Fell together in the face.* συμπίπτω is *to fall together* — of armies meeting, of things coinciding. The Hebrew is *his face fell*; at 4:6 the face is the subject.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[name:Καιν]] and [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the offerings|the offerings, the modes of offering, the sacrifices and sacred rites, the festivals, the victims]] of him not [[held to|held to, offered, brought to, turned to, turned the mind to, gave heed to]]. and [[gave pain to|gave pain to, pained, distressed, grieved, vexed, annoyed]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Καιν]] [[very|very, exceedingly, very much, overmuch]], and [[fell together|fell together, met in battle and came to blows, fell in with and met, fell upon and happened, concurred]] [[to the face|to the face, to the visage, to the countenance, to the look, to the outward appearance]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ Καιν Ἵνα τί περίλυπος ἐγένου, καὶ ἵνα τί συνέπεσεν τὸ πρόσωπόν σου;
hint: Why, in Greek, is 'in order that what?'

notes.text: *In order that what?* — ἵνα τί γένηται, *that what may happen*: the Greek idiom for *why*, which the New Testament prints as one word, ἱνατί. ἵνα takes its conjunction sense, and τί stands as plain text.
*Deeply grieved*, Middle Liddell's one sense, so plain text. It is the word of Mark 14:34, Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] to [[name:Καιν]] [[that|that, in order that]] what deeply grieved [[you came into being|you came to be, you arose, you were brought into existence]], and [[that|that, in order that]] what [[fell together|fell together, met in battle and came to blows, fell in with and met, fell upon and happened, concurred]] [[the face|the face, the visage, the countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance]] of you?

greek: οὐκ, ἐὰν ὀρθῶς προσενέγκῃς, ὀρθῶς δὲ μὴ διέλῃς, ἥμαρτες; ἡσύχασον· πρὸς σὲ ἡ ἀποστροφὴ αὐτοῦ, καὶ σὺ ἄρξεις αὐτοῦ.
hint: The Hebrew has sin crouching at the door; the Greek has a sacrifice wrongly divided.

notes.lemma: ἐὰν ὀρθῶς προσενέγκῃς, ὀρθῶς δὲ μὴ διέλῃς, ἥμαρτες; ἡσύχασον
notes.text: *If you brought it rightly but did not divide it rightly, did you not sin? Be still.* [[flag]] The Hebrew reads *if you do well, is there not a lifting up? and if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door* — *lappetaḥ ḥaṭṭāʾt rōbēṣ*. The Greek has an offering correctly brought and wrongly cut: διαιρέω, *to take one from another, divide into parts*. Where the Hebrew has *sin* as a noun lying in wait, the Greek has ἥμαρτες, a verb in a question; where the Hebrew has it *crouching*, the Greek has ἡσύχασον, *be still*, said to Cain.
ἁμαρτάνω's first sense is *to miss, miss the mark*, of a spear; *to fail, do wrong, err, sin* comes after.

notes.lemma: πρὸς σὲ ἡ ἀποστροφὴ αὐτοῦ, καὶ σὺ ἄρξεις αὐτοῦ
notes.text: The words spoken to the woman at 3:16 — πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἡ ἀποστροφή σου, καὶ αὐτός σου κυριεύσει — turned toward Cain. αὐτοῦ is masculine; the Greek sentence has no noun for sin, and the masculine in view is the brother.
ἄρχω's first numbered sense is *to begin, make a beginning*; *to lead, rule, govern*, with the genitive as here, is its second.
The adverb of ὀρθός, filed inside the adjective's entry: *straight*, then *right, true, correct*.

reading: not, if [[straight|straight, uprightly, rightly, truly and correctly, justly]] [[you may bring to|you may bring to, you may apply, you may lay upon, you may offer, you may present and give, you may set before]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[straight|straight, uprightly, rightly, truly and correctly, justly]] not [[you may take one from another|you may take one from another, you may cleave in twain, you may divide into parts, you may divide, you may distinguish, you may determine]], [[you missed the mark|you missed the mark, you failed of your purpose, you went wrong, you erred, you sinned]]? [[be still|be still, keep quiet, be at rest]]; [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] you [[the turning back|the turning back, the turning away from, the escape from, the resort and resource]] of him, and you [[will begin|will begin, will make a beginning of, will lead the way, will lead and rule and govern, will rule over]] of him.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Καιν πρὸς Αβελ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πεδίον. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ καὶ ἀνέστη Καιν ἐπὶ Αβελ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτόν.
hint: The Hebrew says Cain spoke and gives no words; the Greek gives them.

notes.text: *Let us go through into the plain.* [[flag]] The Hebrew says *Cain said to Abel his brother* and gives no words; the next clause follows at once. The Greek supplies what he said, as the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Syriac and the Latin also do.
The articular infinitive with ἐν: *in their being* in the plain — *while they were*.
ἀνίστημι's causal senses belong to the present; the aorist ἀνέστη is intransitive, *stood up, rose*, and with ἐπί, *rose against*.
*A plain, flat, open country*, for Hebrew *śādeh*, the field — the word the Greek rendered ἀγρός at 2:5.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Καιν]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Αβελ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of him [[let us go through|let us go through, let us pass through, let us go through in detail]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the plain|the plain, the flat, the plain flat open country]]. and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] in the being of them [[in the plain|within, inside of, and by means of the plain, the flat, the plain flat open country]] and [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out]] [[name:Καιν]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[name:Αβελ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of him and [[killed|killed, slew, condemned to death]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — him.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Καιν Ποῦ ἐστιν Αβελ ὁ ἀδελφός σου; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐ γινώσκω· μὴ φύλαξ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ μού εἰμι ἐγώ;
hint: The word Cain refuses is the verb the man was put in the garden to do.

notes.text: *A watcher, guard, sentinel*, from φυλάσσω — the verb of 2:15, where the man was set in the park to keep watch and ward over it, and of 3:24, where the cherubim guard the way.
μή opening a question expects *no*: *I am not my brother's guard, am I?*
*Where?*, as God asked the man at 3:9.
Capitalised because each opens direct speech — God's question, and Cain's answer, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Καιν]] [[where|where, at what point, how, by what right]] is [[name:Αβελ]] [[the son of the same mother|the son of the same mother, the brother, the near kinsman]] of you? [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], he [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] not [[I learn to know|I learn to know, I perceive, I mark, I learn, I discern and distinguish]]; not [[a watcher|a watcher, a guard, a sentinel, a guardian and keeper and protector, an observer]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman]] of me am I?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός Τί ἐποίησας; φωνὴ αἵματος τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου βοᾷ πρός με ἐκ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The blood is still crying out: the verb is present.

notes.text: *A sound of blood.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is plural, *dĕmê*, *bloods*, the form used of blood shed; the Greek has the singular.
Present: the blood *cries aloud*, and goes on crying. Hebrews 12:24 speaks of blood that speaks better than Abel's: αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ.
The word of 3:8, *a sound*, before it is *the voice*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] what [[you made|you fashioned, you wrought, you produced, you performed, you did]]? [[sound|sound, tone, sound of the voice, cry, faculty of speech and discourse, language, saying]] [[of blood|of blood, of bloodshed and murder, of race and kinship]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman]] of you [[cries aloud|cries aloud, shouts, sounds and resounds and roars, calls on, calls for]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] me [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ νῦν ἐπικατάρατος σὺ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἣ ἔχανεν τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς δέξασθαι τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκ τῆς χειρός σου·
hint: The earth that was cursed on the man's account now opens its mouth.

notes.text: *Yet more accursed*, the word of 3:14 and 3:17. At 3:17 the earth was cursed in the man's works; now the man is cursed *from* the earth. ἀπό is separation, as at 2:2.

χάσκω, *to yawn, gape*: Middle Liddell has no χαίνω and files the aorist ἔχανον here. The earth opens its mouth *to take* the blood — δέχομαι, *to take, accept, receive*, a verb that runs on to *receive hospitably*.

reading: and [[now|now, even now, just now]] yet more accursed you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], which [[yawned|yawned, gaped, uttered with open mouth]] [[the mouth|the mouth, the mouth as the organ of speech, the mouthpiece, the face, the chasm and cleft]] of her [[to take|to take, to accept, to receive, to receive in exchange, to give ear to]] [[the blood|the blood, the bloodshed and murder, the race and kinship]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman]] of you [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of the hand|of the hand, of the hand and arm, of the arm]] of you;

greek: ὅτι ἐργᾷ τὴν γῆν, καὶ οὐ προσθήσει τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐτῆς δοῦναί σοι· στένων καὶ τρέμων ἔσῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Hebrew makes Cain a wanderer; the Greek makes him one who groans and trembles.

notes.text: *Moaning and trembling.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *nāʿ wānād*, *a wanderer and a fugitive* — words of motion, and *nād* is the root of the land of *Nôd* at 4:16. The Greek has words of groaning and shaking, and the play on the land's name is gone.
The contracted future of ἐργάζομαι, *you will work* — the same form as ἐργάσῃ.

notes.lemma: οὐ προσθήσει τὴν ἰσχὺν αὐτῆς δοῦναί σοι
notes.text: προστίθημι with an infinitive, as at 4:2: *it will not add to give you its strength*. ἰσχύς is *strength, might*; Hebrew *kōaḥ*.

reading: [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[you will work|you will work, you will labour, you will work at and make and build, you will do and perform and accomplish, you will work the land, you will earn by working]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], and not [[will put to|will put to, will hand over and deliver, will give and bestow, will impose further, will attribute, will add]] [[the strength|the strength, the might and power and force]] of her [[to give|to give, to grant, to provide, to give over and deliver up]] to you; [[moaning|moaning, sighing, groaning, bewailing and lamenting]] and [[trembling|trembling, fearing, trembling at]] you will be [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Καιν πρὸς τὸν κύριον Μείζων ἡ αἰτία μου τοῦ ἀφεθῆναί με·
hint: Cain's word is 'charge', and the verb for release is the New Testament's word for forgiving.

notes.lemma: Μείζων ἡ αἰτία μου τοῦ ἀφεθῆναί με
notes.text: A comparative with a genitive infinitive: *my charge is greater than for me to be released*. αἰτία is *a charge, accusation*, then *the guilt* it implies, then *a cause*; ἀφίημι is *to send forth, let go, set free*, the verb the New Testament uses for forgiving. The Hebrew *gādôl ʿăwōnî minnĕśōʾ* is as double: *ʿāwōn* is guilt or its punishment, and *nāśāʾ* is to bear or to forgive.
μέγας's first sense is *big*, so its comparative μείζων is *bigger*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Καιν]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[the lord|the lord, the master, the one having power and authority over]] [[bigger|bigger, greater, taller, vaster, stronger and mightier, weightier and more important]] [[the charge|the charge, the accusation, the guilt, the fault, the cause]] of me [[to be sent forth|to be sent forth, to be discharged, to be sent away and let go, to be set free, to be released]] me;

greek: εἰ ἐκβάλλεις με σήμερον ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου κρυβήσομαι, καὶ ἔσομαι στένων καὶ τρέμων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὁ εὑρίσκων με ἀποκτενεῖ με.
hint: Cain fears for himself the verb of 4:8.

notes.text: Present: *you are throwing me out*. Codex Alexandrinus reads the future, ἐκβαλεῖς.

notes.lemma: ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς … ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου
notes.text: πρόσωπον twice: the face of the earth, which he is driven from, and God's face, which he will be hidden from — κρύπτω, the verb of 3:8, where the man and the woman hid ἀπὸ προσώπου κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ.
*To-day*, Middle Liddell's one sense, so plain text.

reading: if [[you throw|you throw, you cast out of, you throw out, you cast out and banish, you depose, you throw away and reject]] me to-day [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the face|of the face, of the visage, of the countenance, of the look, of the outward appearance]] of you [[I will be hidden|I will be hidden, I will be covered and cloaked, I will hide myself and lie hidden, I will be concealed]], and I will be [[moaning|moaning, sighing, groaning, bewailing and lamenting]] and [[trembling|trembling, fearing, trembling at]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], and it will be [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the one finding|the one finding, the one finding out, the one discovering]] me [[will kill|will kill, will slay, will condemn to death]] me.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεός Οὐχ οὕτως· πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας Καιν ἑπτὰ ἐκδικούμενα παραλύσει. καὶ ἔθετο κύριος ὁ θεὸς σημεῖον τῷ Καιν τοῦ μὴ ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν πάντα τὸν εὑρίσκοντα αὐτόν.
hint: The Hebrew says 'therefore'; the Greek says 'not so'.

notes.text: *Not so.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lākēn*, *therefore*. *lōʾ kēn*, *not so*, differs from it by one letter, and the Greek renders that.

For the Hebrew *šibʿātayim yuqqām*, *he will be avenged sevenfold*. ἐκδικέω is *to avenge, punish*; παραλύω is *to loose from the side, detach, undo*. The words are plain and the sense is not: *every one who killed Cain will loose seven things being avenged*.
ἀναιρέω's first sense is *to take up, raise*; *to make away with, destroy, kill* is its third. The genitive infinitive gives the purpose: so that no one finding him should take him up.
*A sign, a mark, token*; Hebrew *ʾôt*. Neither says what it was.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to him [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] not [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much]]; [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the one having killed|the one having killed, the one having slain]] [[name:Καιν]] seven [[things being avenged|things being avenged, things being punished, things on which vengeance is exacted]] [[will loose from the side|will loose from the side, will take off and detach, will undo and put an end to, will set free, will loose beside]]. and [[set|set, put, placed, planted, laid]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[a sign|a sign, a mark and token, a sign from the gods and an omen, a signal, a standard and ensign, a boundary]] to [[name:Καιν]] not [[to take up|to take up, to raise, to take up and carry off, to make away with and destroy and kill, to abolish]] him [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the one finding|the one finding, the one finding out, the one discovering]] him.

greek: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ Καιν ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ᾤκησεν ἐν γῇ Ναιδ κατέναντι Εδεμ.
hint: The land's Hebrew name means wandering, and the Greek only transliterates it.

notes.text: Hebrew *Nôd*, *wandering* — the root of the *nād* of 4:12, which the Greek rendered τρέμων. Transliterated, it names a land and no longer says what Cain is.
*Over against Eden*; Hebrew *qidmat-ʿēden*, *east of Eden*. Εδεμ is glossed again, first in this chapter.
οἰκέω, *to inhabit, occupy*; *to dwell, live, be settled* is its second sense.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[went out of|went out of, came out, went away and marched off, went forth]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Καιν]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] and [[inhabited|inhabited, occupied, dwelt and lived, was settled]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, the ground]] of [[name:Ναιδ]] [[over against|over against, opposite, before]] [[name:Εδεμ]].

greek: Καὶ ἔγνω Καιν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτεκεν τὸν Ενωχ· καὶ ἦν οἰκοδομῶν πόλιν καὶ ἐπωνόμασεν τὴν πόλιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ενωχ.
hint: The first city in the book is built by Cain.

notes.text: Imperfect with a participle, *was building*: the work under way, not finished. οἰκοδομέω, *to build a house*, the verb of the rib at 2:22.
ἐπονομάζω, *to give a surname, to name*, with ἐπί and ὄνομα: the city is named *upon* the son's name.
Hebrew *Ḥănôk*, usually connected with *ḥānak*, *to dedicate*. Seth's descendant at 5:18 has the same name, and the Greek spells both alike.

reading: And [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Καιν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of him, and [[having collected|having collected, having gathered together, having taken up, having laid hold of and seized, having comprehended, having conceived]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] [[name:Ενωχ]]; and was, and kept on being, [[building a house|building a house, building, building for himself]] [[a city|a city, a citadel, a country, a body of citizens, a state]] and [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of the son of him [[name:Ενωχ]].

names.gloss: (Ενωχ, from Hebrew Ḥănôk, usually connected with ḥānak, "to dedicate")

greek: ἐγενήθη δὲ τῷ Ενωχ Γαιδαδ, καὶ Γαιδαδ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μαιηλ, καὶ Μαιηλ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μαθουσαλα, καὶ Μαθουσαλα ἐγέννησεν τὸν Λαμεχ.
hint: The Greek gives Cain's descendant the name of Seth's.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew names this man *Mĕtûšāʾēl*, and Seth's descendant at 5:21 *Mĕtûšelaḥ* — two names. The Greek gives both the one name, Μαθουσαλα; with Ενωχ and Λαμεχ in both lines as well, Cain's line and Seth's read more alike in Greek than in Hebrew.
Aorist passive of γίνομαι, *came into being*, where the Hebrew has *wayyiwwālēd*, *was born*. The same entry as ἐγένετο.
Hebrew *ʿÎrād*, *Mĕḥûyāʾēl* and *Lemek*. In Γαιδαδ, Γ renders the Hebrew *ʿayin*, as in Γομορρα, and δ stands where the Hebrew has *r* — two letters easily confused.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] to [[name:Ενωχ]] [[name:Γαιδαδ]], and [[name:Γαιδαδ]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Μαιηλ]], and [[name:Μαιηλ]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Μαθουσαλα]], and [[name:Μαθουσαλα]] [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[name:Λαμεχ]].

names.gloss: (Γαιδαδ, from Hebrew ʿÎrād, of uncertain meaning)
(Μαιηλ, from Hebrew Mĕḥûyāʾēl, of uncertain meaning, ending in ʾēl, "God")
(Μαθουσαλα, the Greek form of Hebrew Mĕtûšelaḥ at 5:21, given here for Mĕtûšāʾēl, usually explained as "man of God")
(Λαμεχ, from Hebrew Lemek, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἔλαβεν ἑαυτῷ Λαμεχ δύο γυναῖκας, ὄνομα τῇ μιᾷ Αδα, καὶ ὄνομα τῇ δευτέρᾳ Σελλα.
hint: The first man in the book with two wives.

notes.text: γυνή is *a woman* and *a wife*, one word for both, as the Hebrew *ʾiššâ* is.
No verb, as at 2:11: *a name to the one*.
Hebrew *ʿĀdâ*, usually connected with *ornament*, and *Ṣillâ*, with *shade*.

reading: and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — for himself [[name:Λαμεχ]] two [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women]], [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the one|to the one, to a single one, to one alone]] [[name:Αδα]], and [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] to the second [[name:Σελλα]].

names.gloss: (Αδα, from Hebrew ʿĀdâ, usually connected with ʿădî, "ornament")
(Σελλα, from Hebrew Ṣillâ, usually connected with ṣēl, "shade")

greek: καὶ ἔτεκεν Αδα τὸν Ιωβελ· οὗτος ἦν ὁ πατὴρ οἰκούντων ἐν σκηναῖς κτηνοτρόφων.
hint: The tent here is the word John uses when the word pitches its tent.

notes.lemma: ὁ πατὴρ οἰκούντων ἐν σκηναῖς κτηνοτρόφων
notes.text: *The father of those dwelling in tents, keeping cattle*: πατήρ as the founder of a way of life, as the Hebrew *ʾăbî* is. σκηνή is first *a covered place, a tent* — the word behind John 1:14's ἐσκήνωσεν.
Hebrew *Yābāl*. Ιωβελ here and Ιουβαλ in the next verse render two names usually connected with one Hebrew root, *yābal*, *to lead, bring*.

reading: and [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] [[name:Αδα]] [[name:Ιωβελ]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] was, and kept on being, [[the father|the father, the grandfather]] [[of those inhabiting|of those inhabiting, of those occupying, of those dwelling and living]] [[in covered places|within, inside of, and by means of covered places, tents, camps, dwelling-places, temples]] [[of those keeping cattle|of those keeping cattle, of the pastoral]].

names.gloss: (Ιωβελ, from Hebrew Yābāl, usually connected with yābal, "to lead, bring")

greek: καὶ ὄνομα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ Ιουβαλ· οὗτος ἦν ὁ καταδείξας ψαλτήριον καὶ κιθάραν.
hint: The Hebrew makes Jubal a father of musicians; the Greek makes him the one who showed the instruments.

notes.text: καταδείκνυμι, *to discover and make known*, then *to invent and teach*. [[flag]] The Hebrew calls Jubal *the father of all who handle lyre and pipe*, *kinnôr wĕʿûgāb*; the Greek makes him the one who first showed the instruments, and names them ψαλτήριον and κιθάρα.
No Middle Liddell entry. LSJ gives *stringed instrument, psaltery, harp* and cites this verse; the word is behind English *psaltery* and *psalter*.
Hebrew *Yûbal*.

reading: and [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression]] [[to the son of the same mother|to the son of the same mother, to the brother, to the near kinsman]] of him [[name:Ιουβαλ]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] was, and kept on being, [[the one having discovered and made known|the one having discovered and made known, the one having invented and taught and introduced, the one having shown how]] [[stringed instrument|stringed instrument, psaltery, harp]] and [[lyre|lyre, lute]].

names.gloss: (Ιουβαλ, from Hebrew Yûbal, usually connected with yābal, "to lead, bring")

greek: Σελλα δὲ ἔτεκεν καὶ αὐτὴ τὸν Θοβελ, καὶ ἦν σφυροκόπος χαλκεὺς χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου· ἀδελφὴ δὲ Θοβελ Νοεμα.
hint: The Hebrew name joins Cain's to Tubal's; the Greek name drops it.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew name is *Tûbal-qayin*, with Cain's name joined to it. The Greek has only Θοβελ.
Not in Middle Liddell, and not in LSJ, which has only the verb of the same compound, σφυροκοπέω, *beat with a hammer*. With no lexicon sense to head it, it stands as plain text, *a hammer-beater*.
χαλκεύς is *a worker in copper, a smith*; χαλκός is *copper* first, then bronze and brass. The Hebrew *nĕḥōšet* likewise covers copper and bronze.
Hebrew *Naʿămâ*, *pleasant*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Σελλα]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] also she [[name:Θοβελ]], and was, and kept on being, a hammer-beater [[a worker in copper|a worker in copper, a smith, a joiner, a worker in metal]] [[of copper|of copper, of metal, of bronze, of brass]] and [[of iron|of iron, of a weapon and sword, of a knife and axe-head]]; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], sister of [[name:Θοβελ]] [[name:Νοεμα]].

names.gloss: (Θοβελ, from Hebrew Tûbal-qayin, without its second part)

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Λαμεχ ταῖς ἑαυτοῦ γυναιξίν Αδα καὶ Σελλα, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς φωνῆς, γυναῖκες Λαμεχ, ἐνωτίσασθέ μου τοὺς λόγους, ὅτι ἄνδρα ἀπέκτεινα εἰς τραῦμα ἐμοὶ καὶ νεανίσκον εἰς μώλωπα ἐμοί,
hint: The first lines Rahlfs sets as verse, and the word for Lamech's bruise is Isaiah's.

notes.lemma: Αδα καὶ Σελλα, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς φωνῆς
notes.text: Rahlfs sets 4:23–24 as verse — six lines, in pairs — the first lines of the book he prints that way. The Greek here is kept on one line, and the lineation recorded here; Αδα and Σελλα open the song, vocative.

εἰς of cause or result: a man *for a wound to me*. μώλωψ has no Middle Liddell entry; LSJ gives *mark of a stripe, weal, bruise*. It is the word of Isaiah 53:5, and of 1 Peter 2:24, οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε.
ἐνωτίζομαι, from οὖς, *ear*: *to hearken to*, one sense, so plain text. It renders Hebrew *haʾăzēnnâ*, likewise from *ʾōzen*, ear.
ἀνήρ, a man, and νεανίσκος, *a youth*, one sense and plain text; the Hebrew has *ʾîš* and *yeled*, *a boy*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Λαμεχ]] [[to the women|to the women, to the mistresses and ladies, to the wives and spouses, to the mortal women]] of himself [[name:Αδα]] and [[name:Σελλα]], [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey]] of me [[of the sound|of the sound, of the tone, of the sound of the voice, of the cry, of the faculty of speech and discourse, of the language, of the saying]], [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women]] of [[name:Λαμεχ]], hearken to of me [[the words|the words, the language and talk, the sayings and statements, the speech and discourse]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[man|man, man in the prime of life]] [[I killed|I killed, I slew, I condemned to death]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[a wound|a wound, a hurt and damage, a blow and defeat]] to me and a youth [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[mark of a stripe|mark of a stripe, weal, bruise, blood-clot]] to me,

greek: ὅτι ἑπτάκις ἐκδεδίκηται ἐκ Καιν, ἐκ δὲ Λαμεχ ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά.
hint: Seven times, and seventy times seven — the numbers of Matthew 18:22.

notes.text: Word for word, *seventy times seven*. The Hebrew is *šibʿîm wĕšibʿâ*, *seventy-seven*, and the Greek can be read either way. Matthew 18:22 has the same pair, where Jesus answers how often to forgive: Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά. LSJ cites the word from these two verses and nowhere else.
Perfect of ἐκδικέω, *to avenge, punish*: vengeance taken and standing.
One sense each — *seven times*, *seventy times*, *seven* — so plain text.

reading: [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] seven times [[has been avenged|has been avenged and stands avenged, has been punished and stands punished]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[name:Καιν]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[name:Λαμεχ]] seventy times seven.

greek: Ἔγνω δὲ Αδαμ Ευαν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ ἐπωνόμασεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Σηθ λέγουσα Ἐξανέστησεν γάρ μοι ὁ θεὸς σπέρμα ἕτερον ἀντὶ Αβελ, ὃν ἀπέκτεινεν Καιν.
hint: Seth's name explains itself in Hebrew and not in Greek, as Cain's did.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew names *Šēt* from *šāt*, *he has appointed*: *God has appointed me another seed*. The Greek has ἐξανίστημι, *to raise up*, and the name no longer explains itself — as with Καιν at 4:1.
σπέρμα, *that which is sown*, the word of 3:15; ἕτερος is *the other* of two.
Feminine: the woman names him and speaks, as in the Hebrew.
Hebrew *Šēt*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[name:Αδαμ]] [[name:Ευαν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of him, and [[having collected|having collected, having gathered together, having taken up, having laid hold of and seized, having comprehended, having conceived]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced]] a son and [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of him [[name:Σηθ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]] for [[raised up|raised up, made to rise, removed and expelled, roused]] to me [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent]] [[other|other, the other of two, another, second, other than usual and different]] [[over against|over against, opposite, instead and in the place of, as good as and equal to, at the price of and for, for the sake of, set against and compared with]] [[name:Αβελ]], whom [[killed|killed, slew, condemned to death]] [[name:Καιν]].

names.gloss: (Σηθ, from Hebrew Šēt, which the verse ties to šît, "to set, appoint")

greek: καὶ τῷ Σηθ ἐγένετο υἱός, ἐπωνόμασεν δὲ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ενως· οὗτος ἤλπισεν ἐπικαλεῖσθαι τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: The Hebrew says calling on the name began; the Greek says a man hoped.

notes.text: *This one hoped to call upon the name.* [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾāz hûḥal liqrōʾ bĕšēm YHWH*, *then it was begun to call on the name of YHWH* — a beginning. The Greek has a man who *hoped*, the sense of *yāḥal*, and no *then*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone; the Greek has κύριος for the name, and adds τοῦ θεοῦ.
Hebrew *ʾĕnôš*, which is also the common noun *man, mankind*, as *ʾādām* is.

reading: and to [[name:Σηθ]] [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] a son, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of him [[name:Ενως]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[hoped for|hoped for, looked for, expected, hoped, thought and supposed, hoped in]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[to call upon|to call upon, to invoke and appeal to, to invite, to call in as a helper, to be called by surname]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]].
